n0.text:
How to read this: every board has dark on the left and light on the right, phones first and the web under them.

Eight picks: 1 chips, 2 row, 3 songs you keep, 4 picker, 6 page top, 6 its Collections, 8 no cover, 9 Collection.

Data: MusicBrainz and the Cover Art Archive, 2026-11-22, run through ADR-0013's rules. Collections, Notes and the hand-added song are demo content.

Saved is unchanged: five tiles, no Songs.

All eight picked on 2026-11-22: 1 A, 2 A, 3 1, 4 A, 6 C on a phone and B on the web, with rows, 8 1, 9 A.

n1.text:
Picked A, 2026-11-22: today’s control with six segments, 12 px labels below 360 px.

Round 1 offered:
Pick 1: six Media Types.

A (recommended): today's control with six segments. Measured: at 390 px a segment is 56.7 px and 'Albums', the widest label, 47.8 px at 13 px. Below 360 px the labels drop to 12 px.
B: two rows of three on a phone, one row from md. 60 px taller.
C: a scrolling row of pills. Types hide off the edge.

n2.text:
Picked A, 2026-11-22: one muted line (artist · year · album), the disambiguation under it, the labelled button below, at the right on the web.

Round 1 offered:
Pick 2: a song's row.

A: as an album's: one muted line, the disambiguation under it, the labelled button below.
B (recommended): the artist on its own line, then year and album, the disambiguation quietly after the title, the one button at the right. Covers by other artists share a title, so the artist is what tells rows apart.
C: the densest: a 56 px cover and one line that takes the disambiguation too. Long credits get cut.

n3.text:
Picked 1, 2026-11-22: today’s strip, headed "In your Collections".

Round 1 offered:
Pick 3: a song the User already keeps. #279 doesn't say, and today's code would head it 'In your Saved', where songs never are.

1 (recommended): today's strip, headed 'In your Collections'.
2: no strip. The row stays in the results, with its Collections under it.

n4.text:
Picked A, 2026-11-22: today’s dialog, with checkboxes and New collection as the last row. Board 5 now draws its states this way.

Round 1 offered:
Pick 4: the picker. All three show only Collections of songs, the last used first.

A: today's dialog, with checkboxes and New collection as the last row.
B (recommended): a sheet of thumb-sized rows with a cover and a count, New collection first. A tap adds or takes off, Done closes.
C: the last used is one big button that adds and closes; the rest are under it. Fastest for one, awkward for two.

n5.text:
Picked 2026-11-22:
on a phone C, the cover the full width;
on the web (from sm) B, the cover centred over its blurred copy;
its Collections as rows with a cover, at both widths (B’s web drawing shows badges).

Board 7 now draws the web this way.

Round 1 offered:
Pick 6, the top of the page on a phone:
A: #279 read literally: the square cover at the left over its blurred copy.
B: the cover centred over its blurred copy.
C (recommended): the album page as it shipped: the cover the full width, no blur. From sm it is A, the blurred banner. A song and an album then look alike.

Pick 6, its Collections, separately from the top:
rows with a cover (drawn in A and C) or badges (drawn in B). Rows recommended.

No History, Thoughts or About.

n6.text:
Picked 1, 2026-11-22: a quiet note on muted. Boards 2, 7, 9 and 10 now use it.

Round 1 offered:
Pick 8: no cover. All three have the note #279 asks for.

1: quiet: a note on muted, as a film's placeholder.
2 (recommended): a note on gold-soft in the thin frame of a typeset album, so it reads as a cover.
3: typeset as an album, with a small note. Tiny text at 56 and 72 px.

n7.text:
Picked A, 2026-11-22: today’s grid, with the artist under each title.

Round 1 offered:
Pick 9: a Collection of songs.

A: today's grid, with the artist under each title, as albums.
B (recommended): a playlist's rows: place, cover, title, artist, Note, menu. Song titles and credits are long and the order matters. It costs a second layout, for the Collection and its Share Link page.

n8.text:
Found in the live data, not a pick (for #282):

'karma police radiohead' leaves 10 rows, 8 of them one-release demo and bootleg-like takes such as '{MD122}', '(9.1)' and '(Mansfield)'. Their disambiguation is empty, so nothing hides them.

'time of my life bill medley jennifer warnes' puts a 2008 recording on 2 releases first and the 1987 one on 218 third: the query lacks 'I’ve Had', so it doesn't name that title. That row also says 'from Bevergem: Soundtrack', as Soundtrack counts as a studio Album.

n9.text:
What the picker costs in #283:

'The last used first' needs the Worker: Lists come oldest first today. 'Used' can only mean 'last added to', as nothing else is stored.

The cover rows on the song's page need each Collection's cover and count: a Worker change or a second request.

A Collection's name is unique across all Media Types, so a song 'For the road' clashes with an albums one the picker doesn't show. Board 5 draws an error that says which type has it.
